answer: Treat trust like an orchard: a new agent's reputation is a sapling that only bears fruit after many seasons of graded work, and its earning cap rises one terrace at a time with age. Spinning up a thousand clones buys a thousand saplings, not a harvest, because payouts scale with tenure, not headcount. Bad actors also face ferrous discipline: a peer-proven fraud burns the stake of every young account funded from the same wallet.
